title: Approved Architecture Review
body:
Overview

This is Manon's original Signature counterpart for Approved Architecture Review inside the Secure Communications Assurance Signature Database, built as part of the Signature ecosystem rather than copied from any outside source. Evaluates approved communications architectures, reliability and configuration compliance. The Signature edition keeps the same discipline as the public edition: every entry states the task, shows the method in full, and carries a demo program that was genuinely executed at build time, so the result shown is a result that actually ran. Signature records are labeled as Signature originals wherever they appear, and they never present a design as an established fact. A design is called a design, a measured result is called a measured result, and the difference is kept visible in the record itself.

How it works

The method in each record checks an approved communications design against its own configuration standard: each required setting is listed, each is checked, and the compliance result is the counted fraction that passes. Reliability is modeled from link history, and backup paths are verified by test, not assumed.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this Signature entry is concrete and reproducible. The accompanying demo program ran at build time and its output begins with: PASS - approved settings applied. The complete program and its full output travel with this record, so any reader can re-run the code and confirm the result independently. The Signature version adapts the public method to Signature conventions: the same checks, the same honesty about limits, and the same requirement that a claim travel no further than its evidence. Where this entry describes a procedure, the steps are ordered and checkable; where it describes a model, the inputs, the calculation, and the uncertainty are all stated; where it describes a plan, the constraints are named first, because a plan that hides its constraints cannot be trusted when conditions change.

Use and ladder

A communications engineer uses these records to prove a configuration is compliant, to find the settings that drifted, and to confirm that a backup path works before it is needed. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple Signature records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records carry the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, this record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. The Signature edition stands alongside the public edition as Manon's own original counterpart, and both editions are linked from the database page so readers can compare them.
demo_code:
# Approved Architecture Review: score configuration compliance from counted checks.
checks = [('approved settings applied', True), ('backup path tested', True), ('access list reviewed', True), ('rotation schedule current', True), ('monitoring coverage complete', True), ('change log signed', False)]
passed = sum(1 for _, ok in checks if ok)
for name, ok in checks:
    print(("PASS" if ok else "FAIL"), "-", name)
print("checks:", len(checks), "passed:", passed)
print("compliance fraction:", round(passed / len(checks), 3))
demo_output:
PASS - approved settings applied
PASS - backup path tested
PASS - access list reviewed
PASS - rotation schedule current
PASS - monitoring coverage complete
FAIL - change log signed

compliance fraction: 0.833
